en: Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us: Humayd ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: Jurayj used to worship in a hermitage, and his mother came. Humayd said: Abu Rafi' described to us Abu Hurayrah's description of the Messenger of Allah's (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) description of his mother when she called him, how she placed her palm above her eyebrow, then raised her head toward him calling him, saying: 'O Jurayj, I am your mother, speak to me!' She found him praying, so he said: 'O Allah, my mother or my prayer?' And he chose his prayer, so she returned. Then she came back a second time and said: 'O Jurayj, I am your mother, so speak to me!' He said: 'O Allah, my mother or my prayer?' And he chose his prayer. So she said: 'O Allah, this is Jurayj and he is my son; I spoke to him and he refused to speak to me. O Allah, do not let him die until You show him prostitutes.' He [Abu Hurayrah] said: If she had prayed against him that he be tempted, he would have been tempted. He said: And a shepherd of sheep used to seek shelter near his monastery. He said: A woman came out from the village, and the shepherd had intercourse with her, so she became pregnant and gave birth to a boy. It was said to her: 'What is this?' She said: 'It is from the occupant of this monastery.' He said: So they came with their axes and spades and called him, but found him praying and he did not speak to them. He said: So they began demolishing his monastery. When he saw that, he came down to them, and they said to him: 'Ask this woman!' He said: So he smiled, then stroked the boy's head and said: 'Who is your father?' The boy said: 'My father is the shepherd of sheep.' When they heard that from him, they said: 'We will rebuild what we demolished of your monastery with gold and silver.' He said: 'No, but rebuild it with earth as it was.' Then he climbed back up into it.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, that Na'im, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, narrated to him that 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said: A man came to the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: 'I pledge allegiance to you for migration and jihad, seeking reward from Allah.' He said: 'Is either of your parents alive?' He said: 'Yes, rather both of them.' He said: 'And you seek reward from Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then return to your parents and keep good company with them.'

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Habib: I heard Abu al-'Abbas say: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As say: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he mentioned the like of it. Muslim said: Abu al-'Abbas's name is al-Sa'ib ibn Farrukh al-Makki. Abu Kuraib narrated to us: Ibn Bishr informed us, from Mis'ar; (H) and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq; (H) and al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya narrated to me: Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Za'idah; both of them from al-A'mash, all of them from Habib, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us; they said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya—meaning Ibn Sa'id al-Qattan—narrated to us, from Sufyan and Shu'bah; they said: Habib narrated to us, from Abu al-'Abbas, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asking his permission to participate in jihad. He said: 'Are your parents alive?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then strive in service to them.'

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Shababah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Talhah narrated to us; (H) and Ahmad ibn Khirash narrated to me: Habban narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us; both of them from Ibn Shubrumah, with this chain of transmission. In the hadith of Wuhayb: 'Whom should I treat with righteousness?' and in the hadith of Muhammad ibn Talhah: 'Which of the people is most deserving of good companionship from me?' Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Jarir.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sharik narrated to us, from 'Umarah and Ibn Shubrumah, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Jarir, and added: He said: 'Yes, by your father, you will certainly be informed.'

Abu Kuraib Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' al-Hamdani narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who is most entitled to good companionship?' He said: 'Your mother, then your mother, then your mother, then your father, then the closest to you, then the next closest.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id ibn Jamil ibn Tarif al-Thaqafi and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us; they said: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: 'Who among the people is most entitled to my good companionship?' He said: 'Your mother.' He said: 'Then who?' He said: 'Then your mother.' He said: 'Then who?' He said: 'Then your mother.' He said: 'Then who?' He said: 'Then your father.' And in the hadith of Qutaybah: 'Who is most entitled to my good companionship?' without mentioning 'the people.'

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—and the wording is Muhammad's; 'Abd said: 'informed us' and Ibn Rafi' said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'You find people like a hundred camels among which a man can hardly find a single mount suitable for riding.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from Thawr, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) when Surah al-Jumu'ah was revealed to him. When he recited: {and others from among them who have not yet joined them}, a man said: 'Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?' The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not answer him until he asked once, twice, or three times. He said: And among us was Salman al-Farsi. He said: So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) placed his hand on Salman and said: 'Even if faith were at the Pleiades, men from among these would attain it.'

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me; 'Abd said: 'informed us' and Ibn Rafi' said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Ja'far al-Jazari, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Even if religion were at the Pleiades, a man from Persia—or he said: from the sons of Persia—would go until he seized it.'

'Uqbah ibn Mukram al-'Ammi narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn Ishaq al-Hadrami—narrated to us: al-Aswad ibn Shayban informed us, from Abu Nawfal: I saw 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr on the hill-pass of Medina. He said: The Quraysh and the people began passing by him, until 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar passed by him. He stopped before him and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Abu Khubayb! Peace be upon you, O Abu Khubayb! Peace be upon you, O Abu Khubayb! By Allah, I used to forbid you from this; by Allah, I used to forbid you from this; by Allah, I used to forbid you from this. By Allah, as far as I knew, you were a person of frequent fasting, standing in night prayer, and maintaining ties of kinship. By Allah, a community of which you were the worst is indeed a good community!' Then 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar moved on. The stance of 'Abdullah and his words reached al-Hajjaj, so he sent for him [Ibn al-Zubayr], had him taken down from his cross/trunk, and cast into the graves of the Jews. Then he sent for his mother, Asma' bint Abi Bakr, but she refused to come to him. So he sent the messenger back to her, saying: 'You will come to me, or I will certainly send someone to drag you by your braids.' He said: But she refused and said: 'By Allah, I will not come to you until you send someone who drags me by my braids.' He said: Thereupon he said: 'Bring me my sandals!' So he took his sandals and strode briskly until he entered upon her and said: 'How did you see what I did to the enemy of Allah?' She said: 'I saw that you ruined his worldly life, and he ruined your Hereafter! It has reached me that you say to him, "O son of the woman with two waistbands!" By Allah, I am indeed the woman of two waistbands: as for one of them, I used to tie up the food of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and the food of Abu Bakr away from animals, and as for the other, it is the waistband of a woman which she cannot do without. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) narrated to us that "In Thaqif there will be a liar and a destroyer." As for the liar, we have seen him; and as for the destroyer, I do not consider you to be anyone other than him.' He said: Thereupon he stood up from her and did not respond to her.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us: Mahdi ibn Maymun narrated to us, from Abu al-Wazi' Jabir ibn 'Amr al-Rasibi: I heard Abu Barzah say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent a man to one of the clans of the Arabs, but they reviled him and beat him. So he came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and informed him, whereupon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'If it were the people of 'Oman you had visited, they would neither have reviled you nor beaten you.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to me; they said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us: my father narrated to us: I heard Harmalah al-Misri narrating from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shumashah, from Abu Basrah, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'You will certainly conquer Egypt, a land in which the qirat is mentioned. So when you conquer it, treat its people well, for indeed they possess a covenant of protection and ties of kinship'—or he said: 'a covenant of protection and ties by marriage. And when you see two men disputing therein over the place of a brick, then leave it.' He said: So I saw 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurahbil ibn Hasanah and his brother Rabi'ah disputing over the place of a brick, so I left it.

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Harmalah informed me; (H) and Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Harmalah—who is Ibn 'Imran al-Tujibi—narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shumashah al-Mahri, who said: I heard Abu Dharr say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'You will certainly conquer a land wherein the qirat is mentioned. So treat its people well, for they have a covenant of protection and ties of kinship. And when you see two men fighting over the place of a brick, then leave it.' He said: Then he passed by Rabi'ah and 'Abd al-Rahman, the two sons of Shurahbil ibn Hasanah, disputing over the place of a brick, so he left it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Ishaq said: 'informed us', and the other two said: 'narrated to us'—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Usayr ibn Jabir, who said: Whenever reinforcement troops from the people of Yemen came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, he would ask them: 'Is Uways ibn 'Amir among you?' until he came upon Uways and said: 'Are you Uways ibn 'Amir?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'From Murad, and then from Qaran?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Were you afflicted with leprosy and then cured of it except for the size of a dirham?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you have a mother?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'There will come to you Uways ibn 'Amir with reinforcement troops from Yemen, from Murad then from Qaran. He had leprosy and was cured of it except for the size of a dirham. He has a mother to whom he is exceedingly dutiful. If he were to swear an oath by Allah, He would surely fulfill it. So if you are able to have him seek forgiveness for you, do so.' So pray for forgiveness for me! Thereupon he prayed for forgiveness for him. 'Umar said to him: 'Where do you intend to go?' He said: 'Al-Kufah.' He said: 'Shall I not write for you to its governor?' He said: 'To be among the obscure common folk is dearer to me.' He said: When the next year came, a man from among their nobles performed Hajj and met 'Umar, who asked him about Uways. He said: 'I left him with a dilapidated house and scarce provisions.' 'Umar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'There will come to you Uways ibn 'Amir with reinforcement troops from Yemen, from Murad then from Qaran. He had leprosy and was cured of it except for the size of a dirham. He has a mother to whom he is exceedingly dutiful. If he were to swear an oath by Allah, He would surely fulfill it. So if you are able to have him seek forgiveness for you, do so.' So he went to Uways and said: 'Seek forgiveness for me!' Uways said: 'You have more recently returned from a righteous journey, so seek forgiveness for me!' The man said: 'Seek forgiveness for me!' Uways said: 'You have more recently returned from a righteous journey, so seek forgiveness for me!' Then Uways said: 'Did you meet 'Umar?' He said: 'Yes.' So Uways sought forgiveness for him. Thereupon people took notice of him, so he set off on his way. Usayr said: And I clothed him with a cloak, and whenever a person saw him, he would say: 'Where did Uways get this cloak from?'

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; they said: 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us: Hammad—who is Ibn Salamah—narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, with this chain of transmission, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'Indeed, the best of the Successors (al-Tabi'in) is a man called Uways; he has a mother and he had whiteness [of leprosy], so command him to seek forgiveness for you.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us: Sa'id al-Jurayri narrated to me, from Abu Nadrah, from Usayr ibn Jabir, that delegations of the people of al-Kufah came to 'Umar, and among them was a man who used to mock Uways. 'Umar said: 'Is there anyone here from the Qaranis?' So that man came forward. 'Umar said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Indeed, a man will come to you from Yemen named Uways; he leaves behind in Yemen none other than a mother of his. He had whiteness [of leprosy], so he supplicated Allah and He removed it from him except for the size of a dinar or a dirham. Whoever among you meets him, let him ask him to seek forgiveness for you.'

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj and Abu Kuraib narrated to us; they said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: my father narrated to us; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; they said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah, from al-A'mash, with the chain of transmission of Jarir and Abu Mu'awiyah, the like of their hadith; and in the hadith of Shu'bah and Waki' there is no mention of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and Khalid ibn al-Walid.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: There occurred something between Khalid ibn al-Walid and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, and Khalid reviled him. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not revile anyone among my Companions, for even if one of you were to spend the equivalent of Uhud in gold, he would not attain the mudd of one of them, nor half of it.'

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, and Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us; Yahya said: 'informed us', and the other two said: 'narrated to us' Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not revile my Companions! Do not revile my Companions! For by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, even if one of you were to spend the equivalent of Uhud in gold, he would not attain the mudd of one of them, nor half of it.'

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu Khalid narrated to us, from Dawud—and the wording is his; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Hayyan narrated to us, from Dawud, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: When the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) returned from Tabuk, they asked him about the Hour. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'A hundred years will not come upon the earth while any living soul present today remains upon it.'

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Abu al-Walid informed us: Abu 'Awanah informed us, from Husayn, from Salim, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'No living soul will reach a hundred years.' Salim said: We discussed that in his presence, meaning every soul created at that time.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Sulayman al-Taymi informed us, through both chains of transmission, the like of it.

Yahya ibn Habib and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la both narrated to me from al-Mu'tamir; Ibn Habib said: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us: I heard my father: Abu Nadrah narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said that one month or so before his death: 'There is no living soul today upon whom a hundred years will come while it is still alive on that day.' And from 'Abd al-Rahman, the keeper of the watering place, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of that, and 'Abd al-Rahman explained it, saying: 'the shortening of lifespan.'
Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated it to me: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, with this chain of transmission, and he did not mention 'one month before his death.'

Harun ibn 'Abdullah and Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me; they said: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: I heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying one month before he died: 'You ask me about the Hour, while knowledge of it is only with Allah; and I swear by Allah, there is no living soul upon the earth today upon whom a hundred years will come.'

'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us; and al-Layth narrated it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Musafir; both of them from al-Zuhri, with the chain of transmission of Ma'mar, just like his hadith.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Rafi' said: 'narrated to us', and 'Abd said: 'informed us' 'Abd al-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri: Salim ibn 'Abdullah and Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman informed me that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) led us in the 'Isha' prayer one night toward the end of his life. When he finished with the taslim, he stood up and said: 'Do you see this night of yours? Indeed, at the head of a hundred years from it, none of those who are currently on the face of the earth will remain.' Ibn 'Umar said: So the people misunderstood this statement of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in what they circulate of these narrations regarding a hundred years; rather, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) only said: 'None of those who are on the face of the earth today will remain,' intending by that the passing away of that generation.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Shuja' ibn Makhlad narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's; they said: Husayn—who is Ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi—narrated to us, from Za'idah, from al-Suddi, from 'Abdullah al-Bahiyy, from 'A'ishah, who said: A man asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): 'Which of the people are best?' He said: 'The generation in which I live, then the second, then the third.'
